newsitem.title: USA: First Union agrees to buy Signet for $3.3 bln -NYT.
newsitem.headline: First Union agrees to buy Signet for $3.3 bln -NYT.

text.p: First Union Corp has agreed to buy Signet Banking Corp for $3.3 billion, The New York Times said.
In Monday's edition, the paper cited "people familiar with the deal" saying First Union will exchange 0.55 of each of its shares, worth $53.59 based on Friday's closing prices, for each Signet share.
With a price that is more than three times Signet's book value, the newspaper said the deal would be one of the most expensive bank mergers in history.
Spokespersons for the two banks could not be reached for comment.
Signet, the 50th largest bank in the country with assets of $11.7 billion, is based in Richmond, Va., the article said.
First Union, the nation's sixth largest bank, based in Charlotte, N.C., has operations from Connecticut to Florida, but has been weak in the Virginia market, the newspaper said.

Recently the Wachovia Corp purchased two Virginia banking companies, Central Fidelity Banks of Richmond for $2.3 billion and Jefferson Bankshares of Charlottesville for $542 million, the article said.
Those deals would have made Wachovia the biggest bank in Virginia, the newspaper said.
The biggest remaining independent bank in the state is Crestar, the article said.
The article quoted analysts saying there will be a lot of pressure on Crestar Financial Corp to sell to a bigger company.
